plainTranslation: Energies that spark and cooperate. Easy physical chemistry and a knack for getting things done together. Failure mode: underusing the momentum. Take on a project or a goal together - this contact likes action.
policy: Governed by synastry-policy. Descriptive, not deterministic; intensity is never treated as obligation, safety concerns override astrology.
note: Synced from authored synastry bundle synastry-authored__19_ (2).json.
summaryDeep:
There is a natural sense that the two of you can get things moving together, but it tends to show up once someone takes action. The support is there from the start, yet it often needs a first step before it becomes real momentum. When one of you gets going, the other usually knows how to jump in and help.

When this works, you bring out each other's motivation without making it feel like pressure. One person starts the engine, the other helps keep it running. You may find that projects move faster, problems feel easier to tackle, and goals seem more achievable when you're working as a team. There is a reassuring sense that your effort won't be wasted because the other person is likely to meet you halfway.

One of the strengths of this aspect is how practical it is. It often shows up in everyday moments rather than big dramatic ones. You help each other follow through, solve problems together, and turn plans into something tangible. Over time, that builds trust. You learn that when one of you reaches out, the other is usually willing to show up and contribute.

The physical side tends to follow the same rule as the rest of this contact. Mars is the body as much as the will, and the attraction here is real but responsive, the kind that warms up when someone leans in rather than waiting. When you actually meet each other, the chemistry tends to be there. It just rarely lights itself.

A pattern to watch for is assuming that because the connection feels easy, it will take care of itself. You may both agree on what you want, see the opportunity in front of you, and still keep putting off the first step. Not because you lack motivation, but because neither of you feels enough pressure to act right away.

The growth here comes from being intentional. Momentum builds when someone decides to start instead of waiting to feel ready. The more you support each other's goals, follow through on plans, and turn ideas into action, the stronger this dynamic becomes. What looks like potential on paper becomes real progress when one of you is willing to get the ball rolling.
